content:
zoe: hit a confusing onboarding bug: generator iterator Next(ctx) doesn't cancel the in-flight handshake in some auth retry cases. quickstart user reported hang.

matt: which sdk? can you paste the repro?

zoe: go 1.20, go-sdk v0.14.3. snippet below. the loop exits after cancel but gen.Close() blocks until ctx deadline. pprof shows goroutines in token refresh backoff.
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey)
gen := client.Generator("gpt-open")
go func() { time.Sleep(100*time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for gen.Next(ctx) { fmt.Println(gen.Value().Text) }
// stalls here
_ = gen.Close()
```

pri: yeah we've seen a few of these. root cause: handshake/token refresh uses background ctx and stays in retry/backoff loops. iterator ctx cancel doesn't propagate.

rachel: two non-breaking fixes: (A) add CloseWithContext(ctx) or Close(ctx) so callers can bound shutdown; (B) keep existing Close() for compatibility but implement it to respect a default timeout env var. both buy time. long-term we should thread user ctx into handshake.

matt: ergonomics thought: the iterator API currently takes a ctx per Next call. that suggests the handshake should inherit the first ctx passed to Next or we should document passing a ctx to Generator ctor. mixing both is confusing.

zoe: agree. newcomers follow quickstart which shows ctor without ctx and then Next(ctx) in loop. they expect cancellation to be global. we should either:
- change quickstart to show NewGenerator(ctx, ...) OR
- make Generator remember the first ctx passed to Next and reuse it for handshake lifecycle (impl detail).

pri: i prefer explicit ctor ctx. implicit capture of first Next(ctx) is surprising and brittle. API: NewGenerator(ctx, opts...) or functional option WithHandshakeCtx(ctx). non-breaking: add WithHandshakeCtx and Close(ctx).

rachel: devex action: update quickstart sampleapp to show both patterns and add a short note about cancelling during startup/auth refresh. include a tiny test snippet showing the cancel-before-close pattern.

matt: runtime action: ensure token refresh/backoff selects on ctx.Done() between retries so cancellation unblocks handshake regardless of where ctx comes from. add unit tests faking slow token sources.

ci-bot: created DE-3010 "go: generator handshake ignores iterator cancellation; add WithHandshakeCtx + Close(ctx) + token-source ctx respect" https://tracker/internal/DE-3010 :white_check_mark:

zoe: i've uploaded a failing gist with a unit test that reproduces the leak: https://gist.github.com/zoe/gen-cancel-repro. people can run `go test -run TestGeneratorCancel` locally.

pri: i'll draft a small SDK patch adding WithHandshakeCtx(ctx) and Close(ctx) as non-breaking additions and a migration note. matt, can you add the runtime token-source change and tests?

matt: yep will prototype. i'll ensure Close() still exists and delegates to Close(ctx.Background()) for backwards compatibility. also add a short comment in generator.go about lifecycle semantics.

rachel: once PRs land devex will update the quickstart and the migration note. also suggest we add a short troubleshooting FAQ entry in the docs: "Generator blocks on Close after cancel" with recommended quick fixes.

zoe: thanks everyone! this has bitten two new hires in onboarding so glad we're tackling it. :raised_hands:
